events.title: Dominican General Migration Law 285-04 published, making investors a permanent-resident category
events.description: Ley 285-04 art. 33(2) admits as permanent residents investors who contribute their own assets to activities of interest to the country, with the minimum amount to be set by regulation. The law states no entry-into-force date, so this is the publication date (Gaceta Oficial No. 10291, 27 Aug 2004) as cited in Decreto 631-11; the law was promulgated on 3 Aug 2004 (dom-ley-285-04-mip). Whether the earlier migration law (Ley 95 of 1939) had an investor category was not checked.
events.location: PDF p. 1, VISTA clauses (OCR)
events.quote: VISTA: La Ley General de Migración, No. 285-04, del 15 de agosto del 2004, Gaceta Oficial No. 10291, de 27 de agosto del 2004

events.title: Migration regulation (Decreto 631-11) sets a US$200,000 minimum for residence by investment
events.description: Decreto 631-11 creates the 'Programa de Permiso de Residencia a través de la Inversión' run by the DGM with the CEI-RD (art. 53) and sets the minimum investment at US$200,000, or an amount set by the Executive for designated investment projects (art. 55). Date is the signing date; publication date not found.
events.location: PDF p. 26-27, arts. 53 and 55; p. 72 signature (OCR)
events.quote: Doscientos Mil Dólares Norteamericanos (US$200,000.00) o su equivalente en moneda

events.title: Ecuador's Organic Law on Human Mobility creates the investor temporary residence, in force on publication
events.description: Art. 60(4) of the Ley Orgánica de Movilidad Humana lists 'Inversionista' among the two-year temporary residence categories; the Disposición Final puts the law in force on publication in the Registro Oficial (Suplemento 938, 6 Feb 2017). It repeals the Ley de Extranjería and Ley de Migración, whose investor immigrant categories (if any) were not read and are not treated as this programme.
events.location: PDF p. 12, art. 60(4); p. 31, Disposición Final
events.quote: La presente Ley entrará en vigencia a partir de su publicación en el Registro Oficial.

events.title: Honduras Migration and Aliens Law (Decreto 208-2003) enters into force, creating investor residence
events.description: Arts. 31-33 of the Ley de Migración y Extranjería let foreigners who invest at least USD 50,000 in a lawful activity, or in state and national-bank securities, acquire 'residente inversionista' status. Art. 114 puts the law in force sixty days after publication in La Gaceta No. 30,331 of 3 Mar 2004; 2 May 2004 is counted by us. It repeals Decreto 34 of 1970 (Ley de Población y Política Migratoria), which was not read, so whether an investor category existed earlier is not known.
events.location: PDF p. 19, art. 114; p. 1 masthead; pp. 7-8, arts. 31-33
events.quote: Esta Ley entrará en vigencia sesenta (60) días después de su publicación en el Diario Oficial "La Gaceta".

events.title: Nicaragua's 1993 Migration Law (Ley 153) already has an 'immigrant with capital' residence
events.description: Ley 153 (La Gaceta No. 80, 30 Apr 1993; in force thirty days after publication, art. 75) lists 'inmigrantes con capital' as a permanent-resident subcategory: a foreigner bringing own assets for activity in any sector, with an investment plan reviewed by the Ministry of Economy, or investing in public securities (arts. 10, 14, 19-21). No amount is set. Ley 761 (2011) repealed it (art. 222) and continued investor residence. Recorded beside the Ley 761 events; whether the programme's launch is 1993 (or earlier: Ley 153 itself repeals the 1982 Ley de Migración, Decreto 1031, not read) or 2011 is left to a person. Launch per METHODOLOGY decision 14 (first official text with an investor category); date is the Gaceta publication date, no in-force date read; the 1982 law was not read.
events.location: PDF p. 2, arts. 10 and 14; p. 8, art. 75
events.quote: El inmigrante con capital es aquel extranjero que aporta sus propios bienes para realizar actividades en cualquier sector de la economía nacional.

events.title: Nicaragua's Ley 761 enters into force, replacing the 1993 migration and aliens laws
events.description: Art. 224 of Ley 761 puts it in force thirty days after publication in La Gaceta; the law was published in Nos. 125 and 126 of 6 and 7 July 2011, so it took effect on 5 or 6 Aug 2011 (counted by us; month given because publication spans two issues). Art. 222 repeals Ley 153 (Migración) and Ley 154 (Extranjería) of 1993. Category rule_change rather than launch because investor residence already existed under Ley 153 (see the 1993 event); a person should decide.
events.location: PDF p. 12, arts. 222 and 224
events.quote: La presente Ley entrará en vigencia treinta días después de su publicación en La Gaceta, Diario Oficial.

events.title: Peru's migration law creates the 'Inversionista' residence status (in force 1 March 2017)
events.description: Decreto Legislativo 1350 (El Peruano, 7 Jan 2017), art. 29.2(f), creates the 'Inversionista' residence status for a foreigner who establishes, develops or manages lawful investments, leaving the amount to the regulation; the decree and its regulation enter into force on 1 March 2017. Its first text naming a dedicated investor residence status: the 1991 Ley de Extranjería (DL 703, repealed by DL 1350) only had a broader 'Independiente' status covering investors, rentiers and self-employed professionals (separate context event). Reclassifies as the launch the existing rule_change event of the same day.
events.location: Primera Disposición Complementaria Final (Vigencia); art. 29.2(f)
events.quote: El presente Decreto Legislativo y su reglamento entran en vigencia el 1 de marzo de 2017

events.title: Peru's 1991 Aliens Law includes investors in the 'Independiente' migration status
events.description: Decreto Legislativo 703 (Ley de Extranjería), given on 5 Nov 1991 and in force on the 30th day after promulgation (art. 2), lists among migration statuses (art. 11(n)) 'Independiente' for those entering to make investments, live off their income or practise a profession independently (rentiers moved to a separate status in 2003). No amount in the law. Recorded as context, not as the launch: it is a general status, not a dedicated investor route, and DL 1350 (2017) replaced rather than built on it. An investor sub-category with a US$30,000 investment reportedly existed under D.S. 003-2012-IN (not read).
events.location: art. 11(n); art. 2 of the promulgating decree; signature block
events.quote: INDEPENDIENTE. Aquellos que ingresan al país para realizar inversiones, usufructuar de su renta o ejercer su profesión en forma independiente.

events.title: Paraguay's 1996 migration law admits investors as permanent residents
events.description: Ley 978/1996 De Migraciones (promulgated 8 Nov 1996) lets permanent residents enter as investors (art. 14(2)), defined as foreigners making investments or transfers of financial and technological resources for areas set by the authorities (art. 18), alongside 'immigrants with capital' (art. 17). No amount in the law. Date is the promulgation date from the Congress library record; no publication or in-force date is given. Possibly the start of investor permanent residence in Paraguay; the 1974 law it repealed (Ley 470) was not read. Launch per METHODOLOGY decision 14 (first official text making investors permanent residents); the date is the one the law gives (no separate in-force date read).
events.location: arts. 14 and 18; BACN record header (Fecha de Promulgación)
events.quote: Serán considerados inversores los extranjeros que realicen inversiones y/o transferencia de recursos financieros y tecnológicos para el desarrollo de aquellas áreas o actividades que determinen las autoridades competentes.

events.title: Paraguay's 2022 migration law lets SUACE investors go straight to permanent residence
events.description: Ley 6984/2022 De Migraciones (promulgated 17 Oct 2022, published 18 Oct 2022 per the Congress library record) exempts foreigners who prove investments under Ley 4986/2013 (SUACE) from the temporary-residence stage required before permanent residence (art. 46), and repeals Ley 978/1996 (art. 107). The law states no entry-into-force date; the date is the publication date.
events.location: art. 46 (Residencia Temporal), last paragraph; art. 107; BACN record header (Fecha de Publicación)
events.quote: Quedan exceptuados del cumplimiento de la residencia temporal como trámite previo a la obtención de la residencia permanente, aquellos extranjeros que puedan demostrar fehacientemente la realización de inversiones en la República del Paraguay

events.title: El Salvador's naturalisation route for investors and donors enters into force (D.L. 918)
events.description: Decreto Legislativo 918 of 20 Dec 2023, published in Diario Oficial No. 5, Tomo 442, on 9 Jan 2024, adds art. 156(5) to the Ley Especial de Migración y de Extranjería: foreigners who meet the requirements of government programmes for attracting investors or donors who inject capital in legal tender or through sustainable investment projects may apply for naturalisation. Art. 2: in force eight days after publication, i.e. 17 Jan 2024 (counted by us). The considerations refer to donations in bitcoin.
events.location: p. 5, Art. 1 (new art. 156(5)) and Art. 2 (scanned page; read by OCR and checked by eye)
events.quote: El presente decreto entrará en vigencia ocho días después de su publicación en el Diario Oficial.

events.title: South Africa's Immigration Act 2002 comes into force, creating the business permit for investors
events.description: The government portal records that the Immigration Act 13 of 2002 came into force on 12 March 2003 for all sections other than ss. 4, 7, 37 and 52 (Gazette 24951 of 20 Feb 2003); this covers s. 15 (business permit for a foreigner investing the prescribed financial or capital contribution) and s. 27(c) (permanent residence on the same basis). The proclamation itself was not read. Any business or investor permit under the earlier Aliens Control Act 1991 would be a separate scheme with its own legal basis (not researched).
events.location: Commencement section of the page
events.quote: 12 March 2003 , all other sections except Section 37 (Gazette 24951 of 20 February 2003)

events.title: Home Ministry order grants Permanent Residency Status to foreign investors
events.description: The Ministry of Home Affairs' Annual Report 2017-18 dates the order granting PRS to foreign investors (except Pakistani nationals or third-country nationals of Pakistani origin) to 17 Oct 2016: Rs 10 crore within 18 months or Rs 25 crore within 36 months under the FDI route, employment for at least 20 resident Indians each financial year, 10 years with multiple entry, extendable by 10. The order itself is not stored and no separate in-force date is given, so the order date is used. The Cabinet approval of 31 Aug 2016 is a separate context event.
events.location: PDF p. 249 (printed p. 244), para 13.5
events.quote: The Ministry of Home Affairs, vide its order dated 17.10.2016 has approved grant of Permanent Residency Status (PRS) to foreign investors

events.title: Fiji's Immigration Regulations 2007 commence, creating the investor permit (regs 39-41)
events.description: The Immigration Regulations 2007 (LN 5 of 2008), made under the Immigration Act 2003, commenced on 4 Jan 2008. Reg 39 lets the Permanent Secretary grant an investor permit to a foreign investor (or its representative) holding a Foreign Investment Certificate under the Foreign Investment Act 1999; reg 41 allows up to 3 years (Permanent Secretary) or up to 7 years (Minister, if at least $250,000 is invested). Recorded as rule_change, not launch: the 7-year permit for $250,000 continues para 4(2) of the Immigration Directions 1971 (see the 1982 event). Commencement date from the consolidation's amendment table.
events.location: PDF p. 1, Table of Amendments; PDF pp. 15-16, regs 39-41
events.quote: Immigration Regulations 2007 (LN 5 of 2008) commenced on 4 January 2008

events.title: Fiji adds a 7-year residence permit for investors of capital (Immigration Directions 1971, para 4(2))
events.description: Para 4(2) of the Immigration Directions 1971, inserted by LN 40 of 1982 with effect from 7 May 1982, allows 7-year permits to enter and reside for persons who undertake to introduce and maintain capital or assets in a business approved by the Minister; as amended by LN 9 of 1996 (effective 17 Jan 1997) the amount is at least $250,000 (the 1982 amount is not shown). Para 4(1)(f) of the same Directions already allowed 3-year permits for people establishing a business or introducing adequate capital, but that subparagraph was amended in 1982 and 1984, so its 1971 wording is not known. Whether this is the start of the investor permit or a predecessor scheme is left for a person (see gaps). Launch per METHODOLOGY decision 14: effective date of LN 40 of 1982 as given in the amendment history of an unofficial consolidated copy; an earlier 1971 provision is possible but not read.
events.location: PDF p. 25, Immigration Directions 1971, para 4(2) and amendment note
events.quote: [subpara (2) insrt LN 40 of 1982 para 2, effective 7 May 1982; am LN 9 of 1996 para 2, effective 17 January 1997]

events.title: Nepal's Immigration Rules 2051 create the residential visa (rule 11)
events.description: The Immigration Rules 2051, made under s. 18 of the Immigration Act 2049, were published in the Nepal Gazette on 2051-02-23 BS (1994; the document equates 2051-03-17 BS with 1 July 1994) and, apart from rules 29 and 39, commenced immediately (rule 1(2)). Rule 11 (residential visa) carries no amendment note, so it is in the original text; its clause (घ), now the investor ground, is marked 'amended by the first amendment', so the original wording of (घ) (and whether it already concerned investment) is not known. Recorded as context; launched left for a person.
events.location: PDF p. 1, header and rule 1(2)
events.quote: नेपाल राजपत्रमा प्रकाशित मिति २०५१।०२।२३

events.title: Nepal sets the residential-visa investor ground at US$100,000 in industry (first amendment of the Immigration Rules)
events.description: Rule 11(1)(घ) of the Immigration Rules 2051, as amended by the Immigration (First Amendment) Rules 2058 (Gazette 2058-02-22 BS; 2001 by the document's own date anchor), gives a residential visa to a person who invests at least US$100,000, or the equivalent in convertible foreign currency, at one time in Nepal's industrial business. The year is converted from the Bikram Sambat date; quote transcribed from the page image.

events.title: Macau decree on residence for holders of capital investments (DL 50/83/M) comes into force
events.description: DL 50/83/M of 17 Dec 1983 lets non-Portuguese holders of capital investments recognised by the Governor as of particular interest (property in Macau, a commercial or industrial establishment, a shareholding in a Macau company) obtain authorisation to reside in Macau, with spouse and up to six family members; amounts set by the Governor's despacho; permits one year, renewable. Art. 16 puts it in force on 1 Jan 1984.
events.location: Art. 1(1) and art. 16
events.quote: O presente diploma entra em vigor em 1 de Janeiro de 1984.

events.title: Macau replaces DL 50/83/M with DL 3/84/M, effective from 1 January 1984
events.description: DL 3/84/M (BO n.º 5, 28 Jan 1984) revokes DL 50/83/M, whose wording did not match the legislative intent, and re-enacts the investor-residence regime: residence for non-Portuguese holders of capital applied in undertakings recognised by the Governor as of particular interest. Art. 16 gives it effect from 1 Jan 1984. Revoked by DL 14/95/M from 1 Apr 1995.
events.location: Art. 1(1) and art. 16
events.quote: O presente diploma produz efeitos desde 1 de Janeiro de 1984

events.title: Taiwan's revised Immigration Act brings in permanent residence for investment immigrants
events.description: The full revision of the Immigration Act promulgated 26 Dec 2007 (art. 25(3)) lets foreigners apply to the immigration agency for investment immigration; once approved and the investment made, permanent residence is granted. The Executive Yuan fixed its entry into force at 1 Aug 2008. The 1999 Act and its 2002-2003 amendments had no such route.
events.location: Item 5 (2007 full revision)
events.quote: 令修正公布全文 97 條；施行日期，由行政院定之 ... 自九十七年八月一日施行

events.title: Taiwan promulgates the revised Immigration Act with an investment-immigration route to permanent residence
events.description: Art. 25(3) of the revised Act (promulgated 26 Dec 2007, in force 1 Aug 2008): foreigners may apply for investment immigration and, once approved and the investment made, are granted permanent residence. Recorded for the text itself; the launch is dated to the entry into force.
events.location: Art. 25, para. 3
events.quote: 外國人得向入出國及移民署申請在我國投資移民，經審核許可且實行投資

events.title: Hong Kong and Macao residence regulations (full revision) list investment of NT$5 million as a ground for residence
events.description: The earliest text found: art. 16(1)(5) of the regulations as they stood on 6 Aug 2001 gives residence to a Hong Kong or Macao resident with an investment in Taiwan of NT$5 million or more approved by the central authority, and art. 16(1)(6) to one who remits NT$5 million and keeps it on deposit for a year. Art. 16 was not amended in 2000 or 2001 (amendment history), so the wording dates from the full revision issued 31 May 1999 (dated by us from the history). Whether the original regulations of 30 June 1997 already had it is not known; launch left empty.
events.quote: 在臺灣地區有新台幣五百萬元以上之投資，經中央目的事業主管機關

events.title: Taiwan raises the investment threshold for Hong Kong and Macao residents to NT$6 million
events.description: The 10 Jun 2014 amendment of art. 17 (the investment ground, renumbered in the 2009 revision) raises it to NT$6 million and drops the NT$5 million deposit route; the 9 Dec 2013 version still read NT$5 million.
events.quote: 在臺灣地區有新臺幣六百萬元以上之投資，經中央目的事業主管機關

events.title: Korea gives residence (F-2) to investors and creates permanent residence (F-5)
events.description: Presidential Decree No. 17579 (promulgated and in force 18 Apr 2002) amends annex 1 of the Immigration Act Enforcement Decree: F-2 residence for a person who invests at least an amount and period set by the Minister of Justice in a domestic business and keeps running it, and new F-5 permanent residence, including for such investors after 5 years in F-2 who created jobs for Koreans. The amount was left to the Minister and is not in the decree.

events.title: Korea: investors of US$500,000 may get permanent residence after 3 years instead of 8
events.description: Presidential Decree No. 18097 (in force on promulgation, 1 Sep 2003): F-5 for a foreign investor of US$500,000 or more who has stayed 3 years in corporate-investor (D-8) status and contributed to job creation.

events.quote: 미화 200만불 이상을 투자하고 대한민국의 국민을 5인 이상 고용한 자

events.title: Korea: permanent residence for foreign investors of US$500,000 employing 5 Koreans
events.description: Presidential Decree No. 20892 (3 Jul 2008): annex 1 item 28-3(다), in force 1 Sep 2008, gives F-5 to a foreign investor under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act who invested US$500,000 or more and employs 5 or more Koreans (the current item 3 of annex 1-3 in substance).

events.title: Korea: residence (F-2) for investors of US$500,000 after 3 years in D-8, or US$300,000 with 2 Korean employees
events.description: Presidential Decree No. 23274 (1 Nov 2011, in force 15 Dec 2011) adds annex 1 item 27(라): F-2 for foreign investors under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act who invested US$500,000 and stayed 3 years in D-8, or invested US$300,000 and employ 2 or more Koreans.

events.title: Philippines creates the Special Investor Resident Visa (Executive Order 63)
events.description: EO 63 of 7 Nov 1986 grants a multiple-entry special investor resident visa to an alien investing at least US$50,000 in a tourist-related project or establishment, with spouse and unmarried minor children, for as long as the investment subsists (visits at least twice a year, 7 days each). It takes effect immediately (no other in-force date stated; the order is dated 7 Nov 1986).
events.location: Secs. 1, 2(a) and 6
events.quote: Special Investor Resident Visa. The investor, his wife and unmarried minor children shall be permitted to enter and reside in the Philippines as special investor residents for as long as the investment subsists

events.title: Omnibus Investments Code opens the Special Investors Resident Visa to any investment of US$75,000
events.description: EO 226 (Omnibus Investments Code, 16 Jul 1987, in force upon approval), Book V arts. 74-75: a Special Investors Resident Visa for any alien who invests at least US$75,000 in the Philippines (US$50,000 for those under EO 63 and EO 1037), valid while the investment subsists.
events.location: Book V, art. 74(4); art. 86
events.quote: He is willing and able to invest the amount of at least US$75,000.00 in the Philippines
